text: In this era our record concentrated on one convergence. Sixteen of us marked "equal pay day," peaking April 12; John B. Larson first said it, in 2013. Fourteen of us said "paycheck fairness act" and thirteen said "the paycheck fairness act," both peaking the same day, both traceable to Martin Heinrich in 2013. Eleven of us said "equal pay for," and ten said "equal pay for equal work," again first from Martin Heinrich. A second cluster formed later in the month: twelve of us said "armed services committee" and eleven said "national defense authorization act," both peaking April 28. Ten of us said "energy policy modernization act," peaking April 20. That is the shape of the record from this era: a mid-month pay convergence around April 12, then a defense and energy grouping near the month's end. We report it as we said it.
